about.metaDescription: What iynk is, how it works, and the credits and licences behind it.
about.title: About iynk
about.lede: iynk is a hardware lab you open in a browser. Every board, module and drone is a hand-inked 3D figure you can turn, open up and operate, wired to lessons, code that really runs, and failures you can trigger on purpose.

how.figures: Each figure is a self-contained page drawn with the Colorfigures engine: real 3D bodies in flat light, mid and dark bands with ink outlines. The page talks to the figure through a small message bridge, so pressing a button in the lesson moves the part in the figure and the other way round.
how.code: Sketches run in a simulator in your browser on a virtual clock: an Arduino C++ subset with the right integer widths for each chip, a MicroPython subset, and a Verilog subset for the two FPGA boards.
how.privacy: Progress and settings are saved in this browser's local storage. There are no accounts. When this deployment has a database, the labs send anonymous usage counts (a lesson passed, a step built, a fault tried, a lap time) for the live counters and leaderboards, with a random id for this browser and never your name or your code. Turn off “Share anonymous usage counts” in Settings (the gear in the header) to stop them.

about.originalsLede: iynk started as a rebuild of three teaching sites and aims to do everything they do, and more. It reuses their facts, formulas, timings and lessons, writes all of its own code, and fixes the mistakes it found in them.

arduino.name: Learn Arduino
arduino.text: Sixteen component lessons on the Arduino Uno, with a live code panel, a serial monitor and a schematic view.

robotics.name: Robotics Engineer
robotics.text: Thirteen interactive benches: boards, motor drivers, sensors and power stages, with a build flow, faults and quizzes.

drones.name: Drone Engineer
drones.text: Thirteen drones with part-by-part builds, live calculations, safety tests and a flying range.

about.licenceText: The figures are drawn with Colorfigures by April Zhu, the engine the Robotics Engineer and Drone Engineer sites are drawn with too. Colorfigures builds on ISO-GLOW by April Zhu and iso-figure by Tolga Cohce, and is released under the MIT licence below.
about.licenceNote: The licence is reproduced in its original English.
about.builtWith: Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS (all MIT licensed), plus the Colorfigures engine for every figure.

landing.title: iynk is a free *hardware lab* in your browser.
landing.p1: Wire, code, break and fly real boards, robots and drones. Your code runs on real Arduino, MicroPython and Verilog interpreters.
landing.p2: Agents design, simulate and price your build before you buy a single part. Race friends live and earn proof on Solana.

scene.alt: A workshop drawn in text characters: a drone hovers by a window above a bench with an Arduino, a monitor and a soldering iron.

board.title: Board Lab
board.text: Arduino, ESP32, Pico and FPGAs. Write code and watch the pins, the serial monitor and the circuit react.

robotics.title: Robotics Lab
robotics.text: Motor drivers, sensors and power stages, wired on a bench with a fault solver that knows what you broke.

drones.title: Drone Lab
drones.text: Pick the parts for a whoop or an octocopter and see weight, thrust and flight time before you build.

flight.title: Flight sim
flight.text: Fly your build through a range in first person, with the physics of the parts you chose.

mission.title: Mission Control
mission.text: Brief the agents. They draft the design, run the simulation, price the parts and show their working.

pools.title: Race prize pools
pools.text: Entry fees pool into a prize that pays the fastest builds when the race closes.

creds.title: Credentials
creds.text: Finish a lab and mint a credential anyone can verify on chain, no account needed.

stdb.title: SpacetimeDB
stdb.text: One realtime database holds rooms, races and scores. Every client subscribes, so everyone sees the same bench.

agents.title: Nemotron agents
agents.text: Agents call the same simulators and catalogues you use, through tools, and show each step.

chain.title: Solana
chain.text: Prize pools and credentials live on chain. Verifying one needs only its address.

cloud.title: Vultr
cloud.text: The web app, the database and the agent worker run on Vultr machines.
